transcript.text: theres a funny smell from my oven when its on

⚠ Stop using this appliance
A burning or hot-plastic smell, smoke, scorching or melting can mean an electrical fault or a fire risk. Stop using it, switch it off and unplug it (or turn it off at the fuse box), and don't run it again — not even as a test — until it has been checked by a qualified engineer. Do not use the oven again until it has been checked by a qualified appliance engineer. A smell only when it heats can be something simple such as burnt-on grease or a spill, but it can also be an overheating connection or heating element, which is not safe to keep testing. With the oven cold and switched off/isolated, you can safely:
1. Look inside the oven for food residue, grease, foil, packaging or anything touching the heating area. This points more towards contamination burning off.
2. Look around the outside and rear without removing any panels for any scorching, melted plastic or discolouration. If present, it points to an electrical overheating fault. If the smell is electrical, plasticky, acrid, or there was any smoke, treat it as an electrical fault rather than attempting a cleaning cycle. An engineer should inspect the supply connection, wiring and heating elements.
ok. it smells a bit like hot plastic or something electrical, seems to come from the back/bottom not inside the oven. the cooker switch on the wall looks a bit brown at one corner and felt warm too

⚠ Stop using this appliance
This is most likely an overheating connection at the cooker wall switch/isolator or its fixed wiring. Brown discolouration and warmth at the switch, together with an electrical/plastic smell from the lower rear area, are warning signs of a loose or damaged high-resistance connection. It could also extend to the oven’s incoming terminal block or cable connection. Do not use the cooker again until a qualified electrician or appliance engineer has inspected and repaired it. This is not a cleaning, setting or normal heat-smell issue, and changing an oven element alone would not address a browned, warm wall switch. With the cooker isolated and cool, do not remove the switch faceplate or oven panels. An engineer should inspect the cooker isolator, fixed wiring, cooker cable, oven terminal block and the heating circuit for the cause of the overheating. If the switch is still warm, there is smoke, crackling, or any smell while it is switched off, isolate it at the consumer unit if safe to do so and arrange urgent electrical attention.

candidates: Burning electrical connection or heating-element fault (medium)
Burnt-on food, grease or a spill inside the oven (medium)
Manufacturing oils or protective residues burning off (low)

plan: Safety: a burning hazard is active. The fixed safety warning is shown separately, do not repeat it. It must not be used again until a qualified engineer has checked it: say that plainly. You may explain the likely cause and suggest checks that are safe with it switched off and unplugged, but never say or imply that a check could make it safe to use, or that they might not need an engineer.
The fault they reported is: "funny smell when the oven is on". Keep to it: never describe a symptom, result or state they have not told you.

Stage 1 (broad help): say what could cause this, most likely first, as possibilities rather than certainties, including simple causes (settings, loading, detergent, installation, or normal behaviour) where they fit. Then give the safe checks that best tell those causes apart (most useful and simplest first, usually two to four), each with why it helps and what each result would mean; or, if one question would settle it sooner, ask that. Do not ask for the model number in this reply. Do not tell them to buy, order or replace a part yet.
